research_question: Can a transparent MuJoCo task-dynamics port reproduce policy-independent PhysX contact responses closely enough to support a zero-shot cross-engine robustness check?
scope: Cross-engine task-dynamics robustness; not hardware validation, Sim2Real evidence, or full Panda robot equivalence.
reference_engine: SAPIEN/PhysX frozen V19 B0, 8 N task definition
candidate_engine: MuJoCo with the same 100-Hz task interface and 1-kHz internal physics

parameter_grid.rationale: The time constants span 0.2--2 control periods while respecting MuJoCo's two-physics-step refsafety bound; damping spans under-, critical-, and over-damped contact; margin spans exact geometry to the 20-mm PhysX setting audited in the numerical study.

selection_rule: Lexicographically minimise the worst, then mean, prespecified tolerance ratio across fit motions.

validation_tolerances.rationale: Force errors use the frozen task-level 20% NRMSE scale; 0.5 mm is one maximum normal command increment; five samples are 50 ms at the frozen control rate; peak error uses the same 20% relative scale.

decision_rule: The selected cell must satisfy every tolerance on both held-out motions before policy checkpoints are evaluated. Failure is reported as insufficient engine equivalence and blocks a cross-engine policy-performance claim.
